content:
Today Apple released its latest Mac mini and Mac Studio models, and at the same time, the company also made minor updates to several of its Magic Keyboard accessories.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes the text labels on the keys and instead uses icons

Apple's Mac mini and Mac Studio have received significant upgrades, equipped with next-generation M6 and top-of-the-line M5 Ultra chips, among others.

Pre-order the latest models now: Mac mini here, Mac Studio here.

In addition to improvements in desktop computers, Apple has also updated the Magic Keyboard lineup, with a subtle change in the new model.

The latest Magic Keyboard removes text labels from several keys, replacing them with symbols.

Apple previously adopted the same approach on the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, and now the Magic Keyboard has the same change.

The following changes apply to all new Magic Keyboard models:

  • Magic Keyboard: $99
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID: $149
  • Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad: $179

Commonly used keys such as Tab, Caps Lock, Return, Shift and Delete have been changed from text to displaying only icons. As for the extended model with a numeric keypad, keys such as Home, Page Up and Page Down use new icons to replace the original text.

Apart from the switch to symbols, the new Magic Keyboard looks exactly the same as the previous generation, with the same USB-C support and the same functions and layout.

What do you think of the change from text labels to icons on the keys? Let us know in the comments.
